transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’m here because I’ve been feeling really restless. Like I can’t quite settle in my own body, especially when I’m supposed to sit still and deal with paperwork or household planning stuff.
When you have to do paperwork or planning, do you find it hard to stay focused on it?

Yeah… I do. I’ll start reading a planning email or even a book chapter, and at first I’m with it, but then a few minutes later I’m just staring at the same paragraph and realizing I didn’t take any of it in.
Did you have these kinds of focus or restlessness problems when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. Looking back, it was kind of already there in elementary school. I had a really messy desk, forgot permission slips a lot… and teachers would send notes home saying I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay in my seat.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or euphoric for several days in a row?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m more keyed up, but not… euphoric for several days or anything like that.
Do these focus and restlessness problems cause trouble for you in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah… it does. I’m not working right now, but at home and with volunteer things, it causes problems. People can’t always count on me to follow through, and I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities because I kept dropping the ball, even when I was really trying.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different parts of your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
Um… I’m not sure. I worry about things sometimes, but I don’t know that it’s a lot or all the time. I guess it depends on what’s going on.
On most days, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?
Not really… I don’t think it’s most days. I mean, I worry sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s a lot of different things all the time.
Did these problems start or get a lot worse after a major stressful life change?
It got more noticeable after I got married, I think… when our routines kind of merged. That was about a year and five months ago.
Before you got married, were these focus and restlessness problems already causing significant trouble in your day-to-day life as an adult?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I managed, but it did cause problems. People at home and in volunteer stuff couldn’t really count on me sometimes, and I’ve had to back out of responsibilities because I kept dropping the ball, even when I was trying.
Do these focus and restlessness problems also happen during times when your marriage is not stressful?
I’m not totally sure. I mean… I think it can, but I haven’t really separated it out that way in my head.
When things are going smoothly in your marriage, do you still have these focus and restlessness problems?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid attention to it that way… like separating the marriage stuff from everything else.
When you’re away from your spouse for a few days, do you still have the same trouble focusing and sitting still?

Yeah… I think so. Even when I’m not around him, I still get that feeling like I can’t really settle in my own body, especially if I’m supposed to sit down and deal with paperwork or household planning stuff.
Have these focus and restlessness problems ever caused trouble for you in school or at a job?

Not really school or a job right now, but… it has caused problems. People at home and in volunteer things can’t always count on me, and I’ve had to back out of some responsibilities because I keep dropping the ball, even when I’m trying.
